entities.evidence: יַהְוֶה explicitly names the God who made humankind. The source tag LORD@Gen.1.1 identifies the same bearer as the existing Yahweh proposal.

new.description: The God of Israel, who built the rib taken from the man into a woman and brought her to the man.
new.name: Yahweh

review.translation: [So|0] [Yahweh|1] [regretted|0] [that|2] [he had made|3] [humankind|5,4] [on the earth|6], [and he grieved|7] [in|8] [his heart|9].

analysis.evidence: Yahweh is the subject. The כִּי clause identifies what he regretted: he had made humankind on earth. The following words וַיִּתְעַצֵּב אֶל לִבּוֹ describe the grief he felt in his heart.
analysis.morphology: Niphal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ.

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה names the subject of וַיִּנָּחֶם, “regretted.” The כִּי clause gives the reason for his regret: he had made humankind on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Proper noun, masculine singular, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: The clause כִּי עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם בָּאָרֶץ gives the content of Yahweh’s regret in וַיִּנָּחֶם יַהְוֶה: he regretted that he had made humankind on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected conjunction with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: that (what is seen, known or said)

analysis.evidence: יַהְוֶה is the subject, and אֶת marks הָאָדָם as the direct object. The כִּי clause states what YHWH regretted: he had made humankind on the earth.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, with no prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In כִּי עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם בָּאָרֶץ, אֶת marks הָאָדָם ‘humankind’ as the definite direct object of עָשָׂה ‘made’.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם בָּאָרֶץ, אֶת marks הָאָדָם as the object of עָשָׂה. YHWH regrets having made humankind on earth. The singular noun with the article refers to humanity collectively.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular absolute common noun with the prefixed definite article הָ־, used collectively.

analysis.evidence: In עָשָׂה אֶת הָאָדָם בָּאָרֶץ, הָאָדָם is the object of עָשָׂה, and בָּאָרֶץ identifies where יהוה made humankind. The earth is the setting of human life.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, singular absolute, with locative בְּ and the definite article fused as בָּ.

analysis.evidence: The subject is יהוה, whose regret at having made humankind is expressed by וַיִּנָּחֶם. The phrase אֶל־לִבּוֹ places the grief in his own heart, supporting the Hitpael sense of experiencing grief.
analysis.morphology: Hitpael wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיִּתְעַצֵּב אֶל לִבּוֹ, “he grieved in his heart,” אֶל introduces לִבּוֹ as the inner location of the grief.
In וַיִּתְעַצֵּב אֶל לִבּוֹ, the suffix refers to Yahweh, and וַיִּתְעַצֵּב identifies grief as what he felt in his heart.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in construct with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.
analysis.sense: feeling: joy and grief, desire and anger
